metadata.name: Modified Hoehn and Yahr Staging Scale
metadata.summary: 8-stage global clinical staging scale (0–5) for Parkinson's disease motor progression and postural instability.
clinical_pearls: Document whether staging was performed in the medication ON or OFF state.

options.label: Bilateral involvement without impairment of balance
Mild bilateral disease with recovery on pull test
Mild-to-moderate bilateral disease; some postural instability; physically independent
Severe disability; still able to walk or stand unassisted
Wheelchair bound or bedridden unless aided

interpretation.label: Early / Unilateral Disease (Stage 0–1.5)
interpretation.summary: No signs or unilateral/axial involvement without bilateral limb disease.

interpretation.label: Bilateral Without Significant Instability (Stage 2–2.5)
interpretation.summary: Bilateral motor signs with preserved balance or spontaneous recovery on pull test.

interpretation.label: Postural Instability Milestone (Stage 3)
interpretation.summary: Impaired postural reflexes (unable to recover on pull test) but still physically independent.

interpretation.label: Advanced / Severe Disability (Stage 4–5)
interpretation.summary: Severe functional limitation or wheelchair/bedbound without assistance.

assessment_guides.title: Pull Test: Stage 2.5 vs Stage 3
bedside_steps: Stand behind the patient, warn them, and give a brisk backward pull at the shoulders.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Taking 3+ backward steps but recovering balance unaided -> Stage 2.5.
Would fall if not caught by the examiner -> Stage 3 (provided still physically independent in ADLs).

references.citation: Goetz CG, Poewe W, Rascol O, et al. Movement Disorder Society Task Force report on the Hoehn and Yahr staging scale: status and recommendations. Mov Disord. 2004;19(9):1020-1028.
